% DRIFT formal specification -- the saturable (Michaelis-Menten) flux.
%
% The source of truth is DRIFT's code:
%   drift/metabolic.py :: michaelis_menten_mapping
%       x * (km + 1) / (km + x)
%   drift/metabolic.py :: MetabolicBridge.get_constraints_with_scalings
%       constraints[reaction] = -(base_vmax * scaling)
%
% The machine-checkable block below is GENERATED by
%   python3 scripts/export_drift_to_qed.py --spec-sync
% and is verified by
%   python3 scripts/verify_drift_lemmas.py <lemmas> --strict
% which drives QED.
%
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
% THE MAPPING IS THE NORMALIZED FORM, NOT THE TEXTBOOK FRACTION.
%
% The implementation returns
%     f(C) = C * (Km + 1) / (Km + C),
% not C / (Km + C).  An earlier version of this spec certified the
% textbook fraction and therefore certified an equation the code does not
% implement -- at C = 1, Km = 0.5 the code returns 1.0 while C/(Km+C) is
% 0.667.  The lemmas below carry the (Km + 1) factor so the certificate is
% about the code.
%
% THEOREM 1 (decomposition).  For Km + C != 0,
%     C*(Km + 1)/(Km + C) = C/(Km + C) + C*Km/(Km + C).
%
% THEOREM 2 (defining identity).  For Km + C != 0,
%     (C*(Km + 1)/(Km + C)) * (Km + C) = C*(Km + 1).
%
% THEOREM 3 (cancellation).  For Km + 1 > 0 and Km + C != 0,
%     (C*(Km + 1)/(Km + C)) / (Km + 1) = C/(Km + C).
%
% THEOREM 4 (capacity scaling).  For Km + C != 0,
%     Vmax*C*(Km + 1)/(Km + C)
%         = Vmax*C/(Km + C) + Vmax*C*Km/(Km + C).
%
% NO UNIVERSAL UPPER BOUND IS CLAIMED.  The normalized mapping exceeds one
% for large C (at C = 10, Km = 0.5 it is ~1.43), so a claim "0 <= f <= 1"
% would be false for this code.  The bound that survives is the
% decomposition above; the unit-budget identity belongs to the textbook
% fraction, which this repository does not implement.
%% QED-BEGIN
%% QED C_flux * (Km + 1) / (Km + C_flux) = C_flux / (Km + C_flux) + C_flux * Km / (Km + C_flux)
%% QED C_flux * (Km + 1) / (Km + C_flux) * (Km + C_flux) = C_flux * (Km + 1)
%% QED C_flux * (Km + 1) / (Km + C_flux) / (Km + 1) = C_flux / (Km + C_flux)
%% QED Vmax * C_flux * (Km + 1) / (Km + C_flux) = Vmax * C_flux / (Km + C_flux) + Vmax * C_flux * Km / (Km + C_flux)
%% QED-END
